description: baseline: unchanged code, harness and guards in place

asi.estimator: min-of-3 per card, summed. process_time is quantised to Windows' 15.6ms tick and counts numpy threads; canary-normalisation held 6% on one batch and blew to 61% on the next.
asi.priority: ABOVE_NORMAL scheduling was the real fix - same code went 10.5-11.7s to 6.8-7.6s on a busy desktop. canary_mean ~36 means quiet, >55 means contended.
asi.noise: ~12% floor on card_ms_total. rows_to_python/service_calls/bytes_total are exact and arbitrate.
asi.shape: 7d and patterns each hydrate 20,159 rows; today 2,518; last_12h 1,439. Patterns then groups to hour-of-day and discards the resolution - 168 hourly buckets carry the same heatmap.
asi.guard: fidelity.py negative-tested: plotting 5-minute means fails with 'last_7d/pm25: peak lost - plotted 51.9, true 57.3'.
asi.insight: min-of-3 per card, summed. process_time is quantised to Windows' 15.6ms tick and counts numpy threads; canary-normalisation held 6% on one batch and blew to 61% on the next.

description: reduce the window frame in SQL with a point budget; carry per-bucket min/max so the peak survives

asi.where: Most of the saving is matplotlib, not the DB - 20k points into a ~1000px figure is ~19 strokes per pixel that the anti-aliaser then throws away.
asi.widths: At the deployed 30s interval and MAX_POINTS=1500: last_12h stays raw (1440 pts), today buckets to 300s, 7d and patterns to 900s.
asi.surprise: The min-max band is a product improvement, not a compromise. The raw line could not distinguish a real spike from sample noise; the shaded spread can, and the footer still reports the true 57.3 peak.
asi.smoothing: smooth_window had to go to 0 when bucketed - 13 points of rolling mean was tuned for raw 30s samples and would smear 3 hours on top of 15-minute buckets.
asi.untouched: bytes_total barely moved (619223->586138): fewer strokes, but the PNG is dominated by the figure furniture, not the line. dpi is the lever there, not point count.

description: Subscriptions.themes() - one SELECT for every subscriber's theme instead of one session each

asi.secondary_overturns: The primary metric does not cover fan-out, so this was decided on fanout_calls: 102 -> 3, and now flat in subscriber count rather than linear. Kept deliberately against the usual rule.
asi.confound: card_ms_total also fell 3724 -> 2822, but canary_mean fell 50.32 -> 33.72 over the same interval - the machine got quieter. Do not credit this change for it.
asi.baseline_note: Run 1 was measured at canary 50.32 against a baseline at 36.26, so run 1's real win was larger than logged.
asi.shape: ChatRepository.get_themes chunks at 500 ids - SQLite caps a statement at 999 bound parameters and a popular bot can exceed that.
asi.untested_locally: bot.py cannot be imported here (aiogram 2.25.1 does not install on 3.14). CI's images job is what proves it; the edit was kept mechanical for that reason.
asi.insight: The primary metric does not cover fan-out, so this was decided on fanout_calls: 102 -> 3, and now flat in subscriber count rather than linear. Kept deliberately against the usual rule.

description: drop bbox_inches=tight, set explicit margins on every figure

asi.win: card_ms_total 2822 -> 1984 (-30%) at canary 32.99 vs 33.72 - comparable machine, so this one is real.
asi.mechanism: tight bbox is a second full render pass. ~57ms of a ~376ms card, and it applies to the status and alert cards too - status_ms 180 -> 92, which is on the fan-out path.
asi.cost: bytes_total 586138 -> 610744 (+4%). Cropping was buying those bytes. dpi should more than repay it.
asi.margins_are_real_work: Three visual regressions had to be fixed by looking at the PNGs, not by the metric: suptitle collided with the pane title, end labels ran off the right edge, and the heatmap lost both its colourbar scale and its worst/best-hour line. A benchmark cannot see any of that.
asi.next: Remaining per-card cost is now flat across card types (~250-305ms), which says figure construction rather than data volume. dpi and scaffolding reuse are the two levers left.
asi.insight: card_ms_total 2822 -> 1984 (-30%) at canary 32.99 vs 33.72 - comparable machine, so this one is real.

description: hoist date2num out of the per-plot-call path in window_chart

asi.READ_THIS_BEFORE_COMPARING: The raw metric rose 1984 -> 2854 and that is NOT a regression. canary_mean went 32.99 -> ~50: the desktop's owner started using it. Run 3's 1984 was measured on a quiet machine and is not comparable to anything after it.
asi.controlled_ab: git stash of charts.py, measured both ways in the same minute: old 2995.9/2991.3, new 2854.1/2895.2/2903.5, canary 47.6-54.2 throughout. 3.6% real improvement.
asi.profile: Per 7d card: text layout/render ~115ms (biggest), PNG encode ~48ms, sqlite ~48ms, date2num ~52ms, path drawing ~12ms. Text is where the remaining money is.
asi.why_it_was_slow: window_chart handed the same timestamp series to matplotlib eight times - 2 plots, 2 fill_betweens, 2 annotations, 4 threshold labels - and each converted it afresh.
asi.method: A/B-against-now is the only reliable way to judge a sub-15% change on this machine. Added to prompt.md.
asi.insight: The raw metric rose 1984 -> 2854 and that is NOT a regression. canary_mean went 32.99 -> ~50: the desktop's owner started using it. Run 3's 1984 was measured on a quiet machine and is not comparable to anything after it.

asi.why_both: dpi is the one lever that moves time and bytes together - it drives glyph rasterisation and PNG encode at once, which the profile put at ~115ms and ~48ms of a card.
asi.quality: Inspected at 875px. Threshold labels, end labels, footer and the heatmap colourbar all still crisp. Telegram re-encodes the upload anyway, so density above what it keeps was pure cost.
asi.cumulative: Baseline 6665 -> 1781 on a quiet machine (3.7x); bytes 619223 -> 487238 (-21%); rows 87360 -> 3120; fanout_calls 102 -> 3.
asi.TRAP_do_not_add_a_render_cache: Caching rendered cards would be a real production win but would GAME this benchmark: reps 2 and 3 would hit the cache and `min` would report near-zero. If it is ever attempted, the benchmark must measure the cold path separately first.

description: ReadingRepository.summarise() - extremes and level split in one scan; one session for /api/summary

asi.secondary_win: dash_calls 12 -> 10, dash_ms 167 -> 156. Primary untouched (1781 -> 1851 at canary 32.5 -> 33.1, inside the 12% floor and on a code path this change does not reach).
asi.equivalence: The new test asserts summarise() returns exactly what get_aggregate() and count_by_level() return for the same range - the cheapest way to trust a merged query.
asi.one_owner: _level_sums keeps the SQL form of the threshold rule in one place rather than duplicating the CASE expressions across two methods.
asi.remaining_dash: 5 queries per refresh: latest, series, summary x2, patterns. summary and patterns both build hourly buckets for the same range in separate requests - not shareable without a cache.
asi.insight: dash_calls 12 -> 10, dash_ms 167 -> 156. Primary untouched (1781 -> 1851 at canary 32.5 -> 33.1, inside the 12% floor and on a code path this change does not reach).

description: MAX_POINTS 1500 -> 800, sized to the card's actual plot area

asi.ab: Canary matched 43.4 vs 43.0: 2389 -> 2287 (-4.3%), rows_to_python 3120 -> 240 (-92%), bytes flat.
asi.reasoning: The 1500 was inherited from the dashboard and is sized for a browser window. At dpi 125 the card's plot area is ~730px, so the budget should be ~800. Borrowed constants deserve re-derivation when the thing they describe changes.
asi.what_is_left: rows_to_python 240 is now entirely the status card's last-hour get_range, twice (once per theme). Every window path is aggregate-only.
asi.profile_now: 224ms card = 36ms _frame, 19ms figure scaffolding, ~83ms text, ~21ms PNG encode, rest matplotlib overhead. Figure pooling would recover at most 19ms and risks state leaking between renders - not worth it.
asi.insight: Canary matched 43.4 vs 43.0: 2389 -> 2287 (-4.3%), rows_to_python 3120 -> 240 (-92%), bytes flat.

description: narrow the status/alert query path; render the whole fan-out from one look

asi.primary_flat: card_ms_total unchanged (1723 at canary 32.25 vs 1711 at 31.95) - this change does not touch the window path. Judged on status_ms, rows_to_python, fanout_rows and fanout_ms, all of which moved.
asi.caught_mid_change: The first version regressed fanout_calls 3 -> 5, because _recent went to two queries and ran once per theme. Hoisting it to alert_reports() fixed both at once - the metric caught a regression I would otherwise have shipped.
asi.semantics: spark was 'last 12 within the last hour', now 'last 12 overall'. Reachable behaviour is identical: with a 30s interval the staleness rule fires at 90s, so any case where they differ already renders the stale text card instead.
asi.SQLITE_CAVEAT: _frame's ~36ms is partly a benchmark artifact - get_buckets groups on strftime('%s', ...) which parses text per row on SQLite. Postgres uses extract('epoch') on a real timestamptz. Do not spend iterations optimising that query for a cost production may not pay.
asi.insight: card_ms_total unchanged (1723 at canary 32.25 vs 1711 at 31.95) - this change does not touch the window path. Judged on status_ms, rows_to_python, fanout_rows and fanout_ms, all of which moved.

asi.measured: hinting none 210.6 -> 197.3ms (-6%) but bytes 86.5 -> 90.2KB (+4%). native was slower than the default. simplify_threshold 1.0 vs 0.111: no measurable difference, the lines are already simplified.
asi.why_rejected: Unhinted glyphs are blurrier, which is both why they compress worse and why it is the wrong trade here - people read values off these cards. Bought 6% of time with 4% of bytes and legibility.
asi.dont_retry: Both rcParams evaluated by probe rather than by editing. There is nothing to restore.
asi.insight: hinting none 210.6 -> 197.3ms (-6%) but bytes 86.5 -> 90.2KB (+4%). native was slower than the default. simplify_threshold 1.0 vs 0.111: no measurable difference, the lines are already simplified.

description: Postgres-only tests for the dialect branch every card now depends on, wired into CI

asi.why: Runs 1 and 7 put get_buckets under every chart card. Its epoch expression branches on dialect and only the SQLite branch runs locally - this session raised the blast radius of a bug in the other branch from one web panel to every card the bot sends.
asi.risk_was_smaller_than_it_looked: The dashboard already exercised the Postgres branch in production, so no new untested path was introduced - but nothing asserted it.
asi.no_metric_movement: Tests and CI only; the primary is unchanged by construction. Measured anyway to keep the series continuous.
asi.verified: Every assertion was replayed against SQLite and holds, so the tests encode the contract rather than one dialect's quirks. Docker Desktop was not running, so they have not been seen green on real Postgres - CI is the first place that happens.
asi.insight: Runs 1 and 7 put get_buckets under every chart card. Its epoch expression branches on dialect and only the SQLite branch runs locally - this session raised the blast radius of a bug in the other branch from one web panel to every card the bot sends.

description: round the dashboard series to 1dp, the precision the sensor actually has

asi.win: dash_bytes 52388 -> 50659 (-3.3%). Smaller than hoped - many averages already round short, so the second decimal was not always a character.
asi.why_it_is_still_right: Not only smaller but more honest: readings are stored at 0.1 and rendered with toFixed(1), so the second decimal was invented on the way out.
asi.primary_noise: card_ms_total read 1795 vs 1672, canary 32.31 vs 31.49. This change cannot touch the card path; that is the 12% floor talking.
asi.insight: dash_bytes 52388 -> 50659 (-3.3%). Smaller than hoped - many averages already round short, so the second decimal was not always a character.

description: Window.bucket_floor_seconds - the heatmap asks SQL for hourly buckets

asi.primary_blind: Full-sweep A/B was ambiguous (1708.6 vs 1681.6, canary matched) because the effect is ~0.9% of the total. Isolating the card showed 260.8 -> 251.2ms and 672 -> 168 rows.
asi.kept_on_correctness: Averaging four 15-minute bucket means in pandas treats them as equally weighted; SQL's hourly mean is count-weighted. The change is more correct independently of speed.
asi.lesson: When a change touches 2 of 8 cards, the sweep total cannot see it. Isolate the affected card instead of re-running the whole benchmark hoping for signal.
asi.guard_gap_closed: fidelity.py was checking a 900s frame for patterns while the card drew an hourly one. It now passes the same floor for_window does.
asi.insight: Full-sweep A/B was ambiguous (1708.6 vs 1681.6, canary matched) because the effect is ~0.9% of the total. Isolating the card showed 260.8 -> 251.2ms and 672 -> 168 rows.

description: quantise to a 255-colour palette from the canvas buffer instead of savefig's truecolour PNG

asi.best_result_of_the_run_on_bytes: bytes_total 488210 -> 147838 (-70%) AND card_ms_total 2964 -> 2845 (-4%) under a matched-canary A/B. Both axes.
asi.why_it_is_free: Expected to cost ~18ms. Encoding a palette PNG is cheaper than encoding RGBA by more than the quantise costs - the control probe showed a plain re-save at 28.4ms against 17.0ms for quantise-and-save.
asi.quantiser_matters: FASTOCTREE 17ms / 25.6KB; MEDIANCUT+optimize 86ms / 33.0KB. The default median cut is four times the cost for worse output on flat-colour art.
asi.colour_checked_numerically: Reserved hues verified by sampling the palette, not by eye: level dots exact, pm10 series off by 1/255 in red. The 'band high' probe reporting a large drift is an artifact - that band is drawn at alpha 0.13 so the pure hue is not in the image.
asi.probe_was_misleading: An isolated probe on a stripped figure predicted +18ms; the real path was -4%. Probes on simplified figures mispredict, because savefig's cost scales with what is actually on the canvas.
asi.insight: bytes_total 488210 -> 147838 (-70%) AND card_ms_total 2964 -> 2845 (-4%) under a matched-canary A/B. Both axes.

description: cap the y axis at four gridlines (MaxNLocator nbins=4)

asi.DO_NOT_READ_THE_METRIC_ON_THIS_ROW: canary_mean_ms 71.88 against a quiet-machine ~32. The desktop was heavily loaded; 3289 is the machine, not the code. Nothing after run 13 is comparable to anything before it without checking the canary first.
asi.real_effect: Isolated A/B over today/last_12h/last_7d, same minute: 1110.2 -> 1043.1 ms (-6.0%), bytes marginally down too.
asi.why_it_works: Tick labels were 19 of ~45 text objects on a card, and glyph layout is ~83ms of ~210ms.
asi.bonus: steps=[1,2,2.5,5,10] puts PM2.5 on 0/25/50/75 and PM10 on 0/50/100, so gridlines land exactly on the warn and high limits rather than near them. The chart reads better, not just faster.
asi.method_note: Isolating three cards and timing them directly is far more sensitive than the 8-card sweep when a change is worth less than the 12% floor.
asi.insight: canary_mean_ms 71.88 against a quiet-machine ~32. The desktop was heavily loaded; 3289 is the machine, not the code. Nothing after run 13 is comparable to anything before it without checking the canary first.
